review.tagline: Self-hosted agent that works on its own VM desktop with a patched Firefox
review.summary: invisible_dots runs each agent (a "Dot") on its own hardware-accelerated QEMU VM with a Linux desktop, persistent disk and a patched Firefox that keeps per-identity logins. Dots write their own notes and skills, accept MCP servers, queue tasks and recurring automations, and gate tools with allow/ask/deny permissions. It is reachable via web UI, CLI, HTTP API, Telegram and optional WhatsApp, and uses an OpenRouter key for models. Status is alpha.
review.audience: Self-hosters wanting browser-capable autonomous agents on isolated VMs
strengths: Each Dot gets its own VM with desktop, persistent disk and sleep/wake on demand
Per-tool allow/ask/deny permissions, with pending asks kept in an Inbox across restarts
Accepts user-declared MCP servers and reaches the agent via web, CLI, API, Telegram
Crash-safe: accepted messages and tasks survive kill -9, and cut-short tool calls are not rerun
weaknesses: Marked alpha in the README badge
Requires x86-64 hardware virtualization plus Node 24+, Go 1.25+ and QEMU
No Docker or Compose files; setup is built from source
Model access documented only via an OpenRouter key; local models not mentioned
needs: Needs Node 24+, Go 1.25+, Git, QEMU, KVM or Windows Hypervisor Platform, OpenRouter API key
